Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)  
- Assessment consistent with an acute allergic reaction to wasp sting with respiratory involvement characterized by shallow breathing, chest tightness, lip tingling, and a blotchy rash.  
- Top differential diagnosis:  
  • Anaphylactic reaction to wasp sting – High likelihood due to rapid onset after sting, respiratory symptoms, rash, and atopic history (eczema, allergy). Requires urgent medical attention.  
  • Mild localized allergic reaction to wasp sting – Moderate likelihood, but less consistent given systemic symptoms (breathing difficulty, chest tightness).  
  • Anxiety/panic reaction – Low likelihood; rash and tingling suggest allergic etiology rather than anxiety.  
- No contradictory information between transcript and DDx.  

Management Plan  
- Immediate administration of oral antihistamines at home while awaiting ambulance.  
- Ambulance called for rapid transport to emergency department for further assessment and treatment due to risk of anaphylaxis.  
- Advised against self-transport to hospital by wife to ensure timely emergency care.  
- No investigations or ongoing follow-up discussed in transcript.
